title: Adaptive Servo-Ventilation in Heart Failure Patients with preserved Ejection Fraction and Central Sleep Apnea (VENT-HF Observation) - An observational study
summary:
Background
Many people with a form of heart failure in which the pumping function of the heart is still largely preserved also experience pauses in breathing during sleep. This breathing disorder can disturb sleep and is often associated with high blood pressure. Treatment often includes nighttime breathing support using a device and mask that helps stabilize breathing. However, it is not well known how often blood pressure remains insufficiently controlled in these patients despite treatment.

Research Question
The study aims to determine how often blood pressure is not adequately controlled in people with this form of heart failure and pauses in breathing during sleep. It will also investigate which factors are associated with poor blood pressure control and whether regular use of the breathing support device influences symptoms and quality of life.

Methods
About 300 adult participants from several clinics will be observed for up to two years. This is an observational study, meaning no additional treatments are required. Blood pressure measurements, medical examinations, laboratory results, questionnaires on symptoms and quality of life, and data from the breathing support device will be analyzed.

interventions.name: Patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and established adaptive servoventilation (ASV) therapy for central sleep apnea (CSA) will be asked about their quality of life during routine clinical visits using the EQ-5D, FSS, ESS, FOSQ-10, and KCCQ-12 questionnaires

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Established therapy with ASV (>6 months) for the treatment of
- Moderate to severe CSA (Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) ≥15/h, >50% central apneas of all apneas or >50% central apneas and hypopneas of all apneas and hypopneas)
- History of hypertension
- Risk for HFpEF or presence of HFpEF (LVEF ≥45%, NYHA II or III without alternative reason for dyspnea)
- The patient is capable of providing informed consent and has voluntarily signed and dated an ICH-GCP–compliant written informed consent form prior to participation in the study
Exclusion criteria:
- Secondary hypertension (other than sleep-disordered breathing)
- Drug induced CSA (e.g., opioids)
- Severe valvular heart disease
- Pregnant or breastfeeding people
